title: Income cutoff and subsidy program participation

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) using income relative to the eligibility threshold as the running variable. The key assumption is that households cannot precisely manipulate their income around the cutoff (continuity assumption), which we'll test with a McCrary density test. We expect a discontinuous jump in housing expenditure at the cutoff if the subsidy program has a causal effect.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s27_data.csv")

# Check data structure
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))
print(paste("Number of observations:", nrow(data)))

# Create centered running variable (distance from cutoff at 0.5)
data$running_var_centered <- data$running_var - 0.5

# McCrary density test for manipulation
print("\n=== McCrary Density Test ===")
density_test <- rddensity(data$running_var_centered)
print(summary(density_test))

# Main RDD analysis using optimal bandwidth
print("\n=== Main RDD Results ===")
rdd_result <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var_centered, c = 0)
print(summary(rdd_result))

# Extract key results
treatment_effect <- rdd_result$coef[1]
se <- rdd_result$se[1]
pvalue <- rdd_result$pv[1]
ci_lower <- rdd_result$ci[1,1]
ci_upper <- rdd_result$ci[1,2]
bandwidth <- rdd_result$bws[1]

print(paste("\nTreatment Effect:", round(treatment_effect, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(se, 4)))
print(paste("P-value:", round(pvalue, 4)))
print(paste("95% CI: [", round(ci_lower, 4), ", ", round(ci_upper, 4), "]"))
print(paste("Bandwidth:", round(bandwidth, 4)))

# Robustness checks
print("\n=== Robustness Checks ===")

# 1. Different bandwidth (half of optimal)
print("\n1. Half bandwidth:")
rdd_half_bw <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var_centered, c = 0, h = bandwidth/2)
print(paste("Treatment Effect (half BW):", round(rdd_half_bw$coef[1], 4)))

# 2. Different bandwidth (double optimal)
print("\n2. Double bandwidth:")
rdd_double_bw <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var_centered, c = 0, h = bandwidth*2)
print(paste("Treatment Effect (double BW):", round(rdd_double_bw$coef[1], 4)))

# 3. Different polynomial order
print("\n3. Quadratic specification:")
rdd_quad <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var_centered, c = 0, p = 2)
print(paste("Treatment Effect (quadratic):", round(rdd_quad$coef[1], 4)))

# Visual inspection
print("\n=== Creating RDD Plot ===")
rdplot_result <- rdplot(data$y, data$running_var_centered, c = 0, 
                       title = "Housing Expenditure Share vs Income Ratio",
                       x.label = "Income Ratio (Centered at Cutoff)",
                       y.label = "Housing Expenditure Share")

# Sample sizes on each side of cutoff
n_below <- sum(data$running_var <= 0.5)
n_above <- sum(data$running_var > 0.5)
print(paste("\nSample sizes - Below cutoff:", n_below, "Above cutoff:", n_above))

# Check for balance in near_cutoff indicator
print("\n=== Balance Check ===")
balance_test <- rdrobust(data$near_cutoff, data$running_var_centered, c = 0)
print(paste("Balance test p-value:", round(balance_test$pv[1], 4)))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive treatment effect of approximately 0.15-0.25 on housing expenditure share. This is because housing subsidies typically increase housing consumption by reducing the effective price of housing for eligible households. The McCrary test should show no evidence of manipulation (p-value > 0.05), supporting the RDD validity. The effect should be robust across different bandwidths and specifications, indicating that income eligibility causally increases housing expenditure among qualifying households.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — income cutoff; test for manipulation; local linear; optimal bandwidth (IK or CCT)
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Eligible households increase housing expenditure share
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~25pp increase in housing spend for eligible households
